The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used for variance estimation; therefore, the precise implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. For any re-analysis using microdata, analysts should apply the official PISA sampling weights and follow the PISA technical documentation for variance estimation and uncertainty intervals.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports Uruguay’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving). Uruguay’s mean creative thinking score is 29 out of 60, significantly below the OECD average (33). Students’ relative performance is above what would be expected from Uruguay’s mathematics and reading performance, and 31% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely attributed to mathematics performance (not statistically different from the OECD average). The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution (67% at least Level 3; 15% at Levels 5–6) and subgroup patterns (socioeconomic and gender gaps), plus associations with students’ beliefs/attitudes and school pedagogies, while noting COVID-19-related data collection challenges and interpretation cautions for some countries/economies.
